arguments.value: This agreement says The Victory Portfolios will make shares of certain fund(s) available to Hartford Life Insurance Company, which will use them for separate accounts tied to retirement plans and variable annuity or funding contracts. Hartford will handle the administrative services for the plans, including recordkeeping, reporting, statements, order processing, and other plan account administration. The funds must provide daily pricing and dividend information, and Hartford can place purchase and redemption orders at net asset value, generally through NSCC systems, with same-day payment and settlement rules. Both sides must keep required records and follow securities, privacy, and anti-money-laundering laws. Hartford may not make statements about the funds beyond official prospectus and sales materials, and the trust must keep fund registration and tax qualifications in order. The trust will provide prospectuses, reports, and proxy materials. The parties are independent contractors, and each is responsible for its own role. If a pricing error occurs, the trust will correct underpayments and Hartford will try to recover overpayments. Either party can terminate on 90 days’ notice or sooner for uncured material breach, but existing contracts can keep using the funds after termination. Each side agrees to indemnify the other for certain losses caused by its own errors, misconduct, breaches, or misleading fund disclosures. Ohio law governs the agreement.
